title: Pulmonary embolism
stem: Resus 3. Ms Kwok, 34, flew back from London 3 days ago. She has had sharp right-sided chest pain on breathing and breathlessness since this morning, and her left calf is swollen. HR 118, BP 108/70, RR 26, SpO2 91% in air, temperature 37.4 °C.

phases.title: History
phases.goal: Monitoring on; the story and the risk factors.

phases.title: Treat
phases.goal: Oxygen, anticoagulation at the right dose, risk and disposition, and talk to her.

notes:
Checked against NICE NG158 (Venous thromboembolic diseases, 2020, updated 2023), the ESC 2019 PE guideline, PERC (Kline 2004) and PESI/sPESI.

Assess clinical probability (two-level Wells: PE likely if score over 4). PE likely: CTPA immediately (interim anticoagulation if delayed); PE unlikely: D-dimer, CTPA if positive. PERC applies only when clinical suspicion is already low (under 15%): all eight criteria negative means no D-dimer needed. Haemodynamically unstable (systolic under 90) with suspected PE: bedside echo for RV dilatation, and systemic thrombolysis (alteplase 100 mg over 2 hours, or 50 mg bolus in arrest) if confirmed or highly likely. Stable: anticoagulation with a DOAC (apixaban or rivaroxaban) or LMWH; risk stratify with sPESI and RV/troponin for outpatient management. Pregnancy: test before the combined pill question; CTPA or V/Q; LMWH.

Your notes (vascular and PE summary) use Wells and D-dimer and duplex for DVT — consistent.

Perfect script checked against NICE NG158, ESC 2019, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the wrong options (D-dimer when PE is likely, the prophylactic apixaban dose, thrombolysis). Added: risk stratification and disposition, bloods, and an explanation with safety-netting.

steps.label: History
steps.hint: Pain, breathlessness, haemoptysis, DVT symptoms, risk factors, pregnancy and contraception.

Symptoms.r: Sharp, right side, worse when I breathe in.

Symptoms.r: A little blood-streaked sputum. No fainting.

Symptoms.r: Left calf aching and swollen for 2 days.

Risks.t: Recent travel, surgery, immobility, cancer, previous clots
Risks.tz: 最近有冇坐長途機、做過手術、長時間唔郁、有冇癌症，或者以前有冇試過血管栓塞？
Risks.rz: 坐咗十三個鐘飛機。冇做過手術，冇癌症，以前冇試過血栓。
Risks.r: 13-hour flight. No surgery or cancer. No previous clot.

Risks.tz: 你用緊咩避孕？有冇機會有咗？屋企人有冇血栓？
Risks.rz: 食緊避孕丸。兩個禮拜前嚟過月經。阿媽試過腳靜脈栓塞。
Risks.r: Combined pill. LMP 2 weeks ago. Mother had a DVT.
Risks.mark: Asks contraception, pregnancy and family history

steps.label: Tests
steps.hint: ECG, CXR, gas, pregnancy test, Wells score; PE likely → CTPA.

Bedside.r: Sinus tachycardia, S wave in I, Q wave and T inversion in III, T inversion V1–V3.
Bedside.mark: ECG: sinus tachycardia with right heart strain pattern
Chest X-ray to exclude other causes

Bedside.r: DVT signs 3, HR over 100 1.5, PE the most likely diagnosis 3: 7.5: PE likely. "Straight to CTPA."
Troponin mildly raised; BNP normal; renal function normal.
Bedside.mark: Bloods for risk stratification and before anticoagulation

Imaging.r: Filling defects in the right lower and middle lobe pulmonary arteries. RV:LV ratio 0.8.

opts.mark: Anticoagulation with a DOAC or LMWH
opts.t: Apixaban 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily
opts.dose: 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily

steps.label: Risk and disposition
steps.hint: Stable PE: sPESI, RV and troponin; admit or not.

opts.t: She's haemodynamically stable, so no thrombolysis. sPESI is 1 for the heart rate, and her troponin is raised: intermediate risk. She stays in for monitoring.
opts.mark: Risk stratifies: stable, sPESI, troponin; admits

opts.t: You have a clot on the lung, probably from your leg after the long flight and the pill. We'll start a blood thinner today, usually for 3 months.
opts.tz: 你個肺有血塊，應該係坐長途機加上食避孕丸，令隻腳生咗血栓再走上去。我哋今日開始俾薄血藥你，通常食三個月。
opts.mark: Explains the diagnosis and treatment duration

opts.t: Stop the combined pill now; we'll talk about other contraception.
opts.tz: 你要即刻停食避孕丸，我哋會同你傾其他避孕方法。

opts.t: Come back at once if you get worse breathlessness, chest pain, fainting or any bleeding.
opts.tz: 如果你更加氣促、心口痛、暈或者有任何出血，要即刻返嚟。
